bindings.source: This encyclopedia is the guided index to everything this site knows about Saint Charbel: his life from Bekaa Kafra to Annaya, what the Church has said about him, the healings and devotions, and the places in Lebanon. Start with the long story, then follow any topic.
The long read is his life and history, from Bekaa Kafra in 1828 to canonization in 1977. For children there is an illustrated storybook, and for a quick map of his life there is the short biography.
Who he was, the key dates of his life, and why people pray to him.
The stroke during Mass on December 16, 1898, and his death eight days later on Christmas Eve.
The cells above Annaya where he lived his last twenty-three years.
The few words that survive, and how to spot invented ones.
From Saint Maroun's monastery to the mountains of Lebanon, his spiritual home.
Pope Paul VI, October 9, 1977, with the timeline from his birth in 1828.
The lights after his death, the exhumations, and what the doctors said.
What remains at Annaya, and the fragments carried to parishes around the world.
What is formal, what is devotional custom, and why the sick come to Annaya.
Reports and healings recorded at Annaya, kept apart from those the Church has formally recognized.
Two cases registered at Annaya in January 2026, and what registered means.
Nine days of prayer, day by day, with the traditional prayers.
Its red, white and blue beads and how to pray it step by step.
What it is, where it comes from, and how pilgrims pray with it.
His July dates in the Latin and Maronite calendars.
The monastery, the tomb, the hermitage, Mass and practical tips.
A five-stop walk through the monastery with real photographs.
His birthplace, the highest village in Lebanon.
Birthplace, monastery and hermitage in one route.
Itineraries, maps and what else to see.
Shrines and traditions on every continent.
The holy women and men whose stories this site tells.
Every page here cites its sources. Reports of healings are kept separate from what the Church has formally recognized, and devotional custom is labeled as custom.
Saint Charbel Encyclopedia. Author: Please pray for the person who made this website.
